And while, with oars suspended, we were awaiting its reappearance — look! — in the same spot where it sank, once more it slowly rose. Almost forgetting for the moment all thoughts of Moby Dick, we now gazed at the most wondrous phenomenon which the secret seas have ever revealed to mankind. A vast pulpy mass, furlongs in length and breadth, of a gleaming cream-color, lay floating on the water, with innumerable long arms radiating from its center, curling and twisting like a nest of anacondas, as if blindly to clutch at any unlucky object within reach. items.new: Whatever superstitions the sperm whalemen in general have connected with the sight of this object, it is certain that, a glimpse of it being so very unusual, that circumstance has gone far to invest it with ominous significance. So rarely is it seen that, though one and all of them declare it to be the largest living thing in the ocean, very few of them have any but the vaguest ideas about its true nature and form; nevertheless, they believe it furnishes the sperm whale with his only food. For though other species of whales find their food above water, and may be seen by man in the act of feeding, the spermaceti whale obtains his whole food in unknown zones below the surface; and only by inference can anyone tell what, precisely, that food consists of. At times, when closely pursued, he will vomit up what are supposed to be the detached arms of the squid, some of those thus brought up exceeding twenty and thirty feet in length. They imagine that the monster to which these arms belonged ordinarily clings by them to the bed of the ocean; and that the sperm whale, unlike other species, is supplied with teeth in order to attack and tear it.

items.new: In recent years, Manila rope has in the American fishery almost entirely replaced hemp as a material for whale-lines. items.new: The whale-line is only two-thirds of an inch thick. At first sight you would not think it as strong as it really is. By experiment, each of its fifty-one yarns will suspend a weight of one hundred and twenty pounds, so that the whole rope will bear a strain nearly equal to three tons. In length, the common sperm whale-line measures something over two hundred fathoms. Toward the stern of the boat it is spirally coiled away in the tub — not like the worm-pipe (the coiled tube) of a still, though, but so as to form one round, cheese-shaped mass of densely bedded "sheaves," or layers of concentric spirals, without any hollow except the "heart," the tiny vertical tube formed at the axis of the cheese. Since the least tangle or kink in the coiling would, as the line ran out, infallibly take off somebody's arm, leg, or entire body, the utmost care is taken in stowing the line in its tub. Some harpooners will spend almost an entire morning at this business, carrying the line high aloft and then reeving it downward through a block toward the tub, so as to free it of every possible wrinkle and twist in the act of coiling.

items.new: Both ends of the line are exposed; the lower end finishes in an eye-splice, or loop, which comes up from the bottom against the side of the tub and hangs over its edge, completely free of everything. This arrangement of the lower end is necessary for two reasons. First: to make it easier to fasten to it an additional line from a neighboring boat, in case the struck whale should sound (dive) so deep as to threaten to carry off the entire line originally attached to the harpoon. In these instances the whale is, of course, passed like a mug of ale, as it were, from the one boat to the other; though the first boat always hovers close by to assist its partner. Second: this arrangement is indispensable for common safety's sake; for if the lower end of the line were in any way attached to the boat, and the whale were then to run the line out to the end almost in a single smoking minute, as he sometimes does, he would not stop there, for the doomed boat would infallibly be dragged down after him into the depths of the sea; and in that case no town-crier would ever find her again.

items.new: Thus the whale-line folds the whole boat in its complicated coils, twisting and writhing around it in almost every direction. All the oarsmen are caught up in its perilous contortions, so that to the timid eye of the landsman they seem like Indian jugglers, with the deadliest snakes playfully draped around their limbs. No son of mortal woman can seat himself for the first time amid those hempen intricacies and, while straining his utmost at the oar, reflect that at any unknown instant the harpoon may be darted and all these horrible contortions be set in play like ringed lightning — no one can be placed like that without a shudder that makes the very marrow in his bones quiver like a shaken jelly. Yet habit — strange thing! what can habit not accomplish? — livelier sallies, merrier mirth, better jokes, and brighter repartee you never heard over your mahogany dinner table than you will hear over the half-inch white cedar of the whale-boat, when it is hung with hangman's nooses like this; and, like the six burghers of Calais before King Edward, the six men who make up the crew pull into the jaws of death with a halter around every neck, as you might say.

items.new: Again: as the profound calm which only seems to precede and foretell the storm is perhaps more dreadful than the storm itself — for, indeed, the calm is only the wrapper and envelope of the storm, and contains it within itself, as the seemingly harmless rifle holds the fatal powder, and the ball, and the explosion — so the graceful repose of the line, as it silently snakes about the oarsmen before being brought into actual play, is a thing which carries more true terror than any other aspect of this dangerous affair. But why say more? All men live enveloped in whale-lines. All are born with halters round their necks; but it is only when caught in the swift, sudden turn of death that mortals realize the silent, subtle, ever-present perils of life. And if you are a philosopher, then even seated in the whale-boat you would not at heart feel one bit more terror than if you were seated before your evening fire with a poker, and not a harpoon, by your side.
